- **Words aren’t labels. They’re levers. Change your words. Change the outcome. Thank you to my friend Dr. Heather Maietta for sharing this beautiful video. Even a small tweak in phrasing can shift decisions. In a classic study, when a life-or-death choice was framed as lives saved, 72% chose the safe option. When framed as lives lost? Only 22% did. Same math. Different words. Opposite decisions. Language is the soundtrack to your message. Tone, frame, energy. And behind each choice of words is awareness. Noticing how your message will land on another person. Try these small edits that layer in kindness and clarity: ❌ “We need to talk.” ✅ “Can we grab 15 minutes to align on X?” ❌ “You misunderstood.” ✅ “I may not have explained that clearly. Here’s what I meant.” ❌ “Calm down.” ✅ “I can see this matters. Let’s take it one step at a time.” ❌ “That’s not my job.” ✅ “Let’s see if I can help. If I can’t, I’ll connect you to ____.” When words acknowledge feelings and invite collaboration, people don’t just hear you. They trust you. Words can open space for connection. Or close the door on it. 💛 What’s one sentence you’ll reframe today with a little more kindness? ...more ...more**

- **Made you stop doomscrolling and look, didn’t I? My feed is now choke full of (AI generated) infographics and long form posts about data strategy, architecture and technology. But here’s the problem with it. You’re talking to an echo chamber. The only people your posts are reaching are your peers, who are already neck deep in this topic. Now it’s a good way (for now) to create engagement, but it won’t persuade C Levels to take action. And if you’re a passionate data leader, that’s what you truly want. Let’s face the truth: Senior leaders seldom care about data. It’s not a thing they can touch and feel, and no boardroom spends 10 seconds discussing Azure vs AWS, except maybe in the context of a budget review. But they feel the impact of data every day. So talk about that. Focus on their problems, not tech jargon. Talk to them about the report they wait 3 days to get compiled together, every month. Explain to them the cleanup job the intern spent 17 hours on. Show them, there is a better way. Steve Jobs once tore up draft ads for the iPod talking about hard drive specs and whatnot, and scribbled down “A thousand songs in your pocket”. That’s your blueprint to success. Focus not on the data itself; instead on WHERE data can make a difference to end users. Let’s talk about that. Let’s turn this feed into something people outside our community actually find useful.**

- **In 2021, the WHO had to halt a trial with premature babies. Not because something was going wrong. Because something was going right and carrying on would have meant withholding it from the babies who needed it most. The treatment was skin. A parent's chest, from the moment of birth. Across five countries it cut deaths in the smallest, most fragile newborns by a quarter, and once that was clear it became impossible to justify keeping the other babies away from it. WHO now advises at least eight hours of skin-to-skin a day. Most NICUs in the world manage under thirty minutes. That is the gap the Skincubator was built to close. Nobody disputes the evidence. The problem is the equipment. For over a century we have kept premature babies alive inside a box, and the box does its job by keeping them warm and apart. The one thing most likely to save them is the one thing the design holds at arm's length. One team spent three years mapping why that gap persists, found more than a hundred separate barriers, then stopped trying to build a better box. The Skincubator is the result, an incubator redesigned around the parent and baby together. The baby in the second photo is two days old and weighs 765 grams, lighter than a bag of sugar, umbilical lines still in, lying skin to skin inside it. Decades of evidence barely moved practice. A change to the environment did what the data alone never could.**
